analysis.title: September 2026: First Look on Hedge Fund Performance and Positioning
key_insights: Global Fundamental L/S funds returned -0.55% asset weighted in September versus MSCI TR -1.19%. Beta losses were partly offset by +0.73% alpha, driven by short side gains outweighing long side losses. YTD return is +12.6%.
Systematic L/S funds (the desk's proxy for quant) returned +3.46% in September, the best month YTD, driven entirely by positive short side alpha. YTD return is +19.79%.
Regional L/S returns in September: Asia +1.4%, Europe -1.1%, US -0.7%. YTD: Asia +23.4%, Europe +8.3%, US +8.4%.
TMT L/S funds gained +4.4% in September (+17.6% YTD), while Health Care L/S funds lost -2.4% (+9.9% YTD).
Equally weighted average Fundamental L/S return was +0.85% in September versus a median of -0.55%. YTD average is +13.1% and median +2.5%.
The global book was modestly net sold in September as short sales slightly outpaced long buys. Gross trading activity rose at the fastest pace since May.
Single stocks were net sold, with short sales outpacing long buys 1.2 to 1. Macro products (index and ETF combined) were net bought, led by short covers.
Communication Services, Info Tech and Financials were the most net bought global sectors in dollar terms. Industrials, Health Care and Staples were the most net sold.

US-listed ETF shorts rose 4% in September, led by Credit and Small-Cap ETFs. ETF shorts are 10.1% of the US equity short book excluding index products, in the 2nd percentile versus both the past year and past five years.
Overall Prime Book gross leverage rose 3.3 pts MoM to 309.7% (68th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 0.3 pts to 77.6% (32nd percentile).
Global Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.7 pts to 206.5% (25th percentile 1-year) while net leverage fell 0.8 pts to 52.5% (3rd percentile 1-year).
US Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 1.5 pts to 45.7%, a one-year low. Its long/short ratio of 1.561 is in the 1st percentile over five years.
North America was net sold for the first time in five months, driven by long buys outpacing short sales (1.3 to 1 as stated). Its weighting versus MSCI World ACWI fell 2.9 pts to 17.3% underweight.

Europe saw its largest percentage net buying in more than five years, led by Macro Products, with long buys plus short covers at 2.0 to 1. Europe's weighting versus ACWI rose 2.3 pts to 2.8% overweight (91st percentile 1-year).

DM Asia saw little net activity: buying in Hong Kong and Australia was offset by selling in Japan. EM Asia was heavily net sold, with selling in Korea and to a lesser extent China partly offset by buying in Taiwan.

US TMT was the only net bought US sector group in September, with long buys outpacing short sales 2.2 to 1. Info Tech saw its largest percentage buying since Feb 2025, led by Semis, Software and IT Services.
Comm Svcs saw its largest percentage net buying since Nov 2025, led by Interactive Media and Diversified Telecom.
US Energy saw its largest percentage net selling in nearly 3 years, driven almost entirely by short sales. Defensive sectors saw their largest percentage net selling in nearly 1 year.

US Health Care was net sold for a second straight month, driven almost entirely by long sales. Its long/short ratio of 2.29 is in the 2nd percentile over the past year. Biotech, Health Care Tech and Pharma were the most net sold subsectors.
US Consumer Discretionary was net sold, with short sales outpacing long buys 1.5 to 1. Its long/short ratio of 2.06 is a 1-year low.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds were net buyers at the largest percentage pace since Feb 2025, led by Semis, Software and IT Services. Long/short ratio is 1.81 (40th percentile 1-year). This is observed positioning, not a formal rating.
Largest percentage net buying since Nov 2025, with nearly all subsectors bought. Long/short ratio is 3.23. This is observed positioning, not a formal rating.
Largest percentage net selling in nearly 3 years, driven almost entirely by short sales. Long/short ratio is 1.54. This is observed positioning, not a formal rating.
Net sold for a second straight month, driven almost entirely by long sales. Long/short ratio of 2.29 is in the 2nd percentile over the past year. This is observed positioning, not a formal rating.
Net sold with short sales outpacing long buys 1.5 to 1. Long/short ratio of 2.06 is a 1-year low. This is observed positioning, not a formal rating.

risk_factors: Hedge fund net exposure to US equities is at a one-year low in US Fundamental L/S (45.7%), with long/short ratio at the 1st percentile over five years.
Health Care long selling pushed the sector's long/short ratio to the 2nd percentile over one year.
The report notes its data may reflect only a subset of aggregated GS prime clients and should not be relied on as a full view of the market.
vol_and_positioning: Overall Prime Book gross leverage is 309.7% (68th percentile 1-year, 94th percentile 5-year). Net leverage is 77.6% (32nd percentile 1-year).
Global Fundamental L/S net leverage is 52.5%, in the 3rd percentile over one year. Gross leverage is 206.5% (25th percentile 1-year).
US Fundamental L/S net leverage is 45.7%, a one-year low. Long/short ratio is 1.561, in the 1st percentile over five years.

Europe Fundamental L/S net leverage is 70.1% (63rd percentile 1-year) with a long/short ratio of 2.328 (97th percentile 1-year). Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage is 62.5% with a long/short ratio of 1.975 (87th percentile 1-year).
ETF shorts are 10.1% of the US equity short book excluding index products, in the 2nd percentile versus both the past year and past five years. US-listed ETF shorts rose 4% in September.
Macro Products (index and ETF) were net bought, led by short covers.

North America weighting versus MSCI World ACWI is 17.3% underweight (23rd percentile 1-year, 5th percentile 5-year). Europe is 2.8% overweight. DM Asia is 3.4% overweight (95th percentile 5-year). EM Asia is 9.5% overweight (90th percentile 5-year).
